Unlike standard trilinear interpolation which treats color and opacity as separate vectors, this method multiplies each vertex's color by its opacity before interpolation, ensuring that transparent regions do not incorrectly influence the color of opaque neighbors [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method multiplies each vertex's color by its opacity before interpolation to prevent transparent regions from incorrectly influencing opaque neighbors. Source [S1] explicitly describes calculating the weighted material color by interpolating the product of vertex opacity and vertex material color ($f_{Trilinear}({alpha}_j C_m(S)_j)$) and notes that this prevents 'interface color confusion' compared to methods that interpolate colors without considering opacity. Source [S2] similarly states that to prevent 'color bleeding' (which occurs when independent interpolation causes incorrect blended colors, such as transparent flesh influencing opaque bone), one must 'multiply each color with the corresponding opacity value before interpolating the color.' Both sources confirm the mechanism (multiplying color by opacity before interpolation) and the purpose (preventing incorrect influence/bleeding/confusion from transparent regions) described in the claim.

Therefore, the evidence fully supports the claim.
